accepted.s: The Special (Civil) Marriage Act, 1872 was also known as the:
o: Civil Union Act
Inter-Community Marriage Act
Indian Marriage Registration Act
Native Marriage Act
accepted.x: The Special (Civil) Marriage Act, 1872 was also called the Native Marriage Act.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the alternate name of the statute.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: Under the Special (Civil) Marriage Act, 1872, the prescribed marriageable ages were:
o: 15 years for the girl and 18 years for the boy
14 years for the girl and 18 years for the boy
21 years for the girl and 18 years for the boy
18 years for the girl and 21 years for the boy
accepted.x: The Act prescribed a marriageable age of 14 years for a girl and 18 years for a boy.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the age figures associated with the 1872 Act from those under the 1954 Act.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Special (Civil) Marriage Act, 1872?
o: It permitted polygamous civil marriages.
It provided only for religious marriages within one community.
It provided for monogamous civil marriage and prohibited child marriage.
It applied exclusively to marriages among Hindus.
accepted.x: The Act provided for monogamous civil marriage and prohibited child marriage.
accepted.tq: Use the exact statutory character of the Act to reject reversed or exaggerated descriptions.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indian Christian Marriage Act, 1872 and the Divorce Act, 1869:
1. Divorce may be sought on grounds such as adultery, bigamy and conversion.
2. Mutual consent was added as a ground in 2001.
3. The legislation applies only to inter-religious civil marriages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Adultery, bigamy and conversion are among the stated grounds, and mutual consent was added in 2001. The legislation is not limited to inter-religious civil marriages.
accepted.tq: Find the incorrect scope statement while retaining the specific grounds and date.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: With reference to the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It was enacted in 1954 and applies to all inter-religious marriages.
It deals only with Hindu marriages and makes registration optional.
It makes registration of marriage compulsory and the term Parsi refers to a Parsi Zoroastrian.
It abolished the requirement of registration for Parsi marriages.
accepted.x: The Act is of 1936, registration is compulsory, and Parsi refers to a Parsi Zoroastrian.
accepted.tq: Combine the statute year, community identity and compulsory-registration provision.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 primarily provides for:
o: Religious conversion as a prerequisite for marriage
Marriage within the same gotra only
Inter-religious civil marriage and registration
Only customary tribal marriages
accepted.x: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 facilitates inter-religious civil marriage and registration.
accepted.tq: Identify the central purpose of the statute rather than a neighbouring marriage rule.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: Under the Special Marriage Act, 1954, the prescribed ages for marriage are:
o: 21 years for the male and 18 years for the female
21 years for both parties
14 years for the female and 18 years for the male
18 years for both parties
accepted.x: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 prescribes 21 years for the male party and 18 years for the female party.
accepted.tq: Compare the age figures under the 1954 Act with those under the 1872 Act.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Section 13 divorce provisions
Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Section 27 divorce provisions
Special Marriage Act, 1954 — Section 27 divorce provisions
Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 — Section 5B mutual consent
accepted.x: Divorce under the Special Marriage Act, 1954 is associated with Section 27. Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act deals with divorce under that Act.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure Article or section pairing and eliminate swapped provisions.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: The Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 applies to which of the following communities, subject to its statutory conditions?
o: Parsis, Christians, Buddhists and Muslims
Hindus and Muslims only
All religious communities without exception
Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs
accepted.x: The Hindu Marriage Act applies to Hindus, Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs. It does not apply to Scheduled Tribes unless the Central Government notifies otherwise.
accepted.tq: Test statutory coverage and the nearby exception concerning Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 is NOT correct?
o: Its application to Scheduled Tribes is subject to notification.
It covers Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs in addition to Hindus.
It applies to Scheduled Tribes automatically in every case.
It contains provisions relating to divorce in Section 13.
accepted.x: The Act does not apply to Scheduled Tribes unless the Central Government directs otherwise by notification.
accepted.tq: Find the absolute scope claim that ignores the statutory exception.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: The Portuguese Civil Code, 1867 in force in Goa is regarded as:
o: A personal law applicable exclusively to Parsis
A form of common civil code
A customary tribal code only
A code dealing only with divorce and not marriage
accepted.x: The Portuguese Civil Code, 1867 operating in Goa is regarded as a form of common civil code.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal character of the Goa civil code.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: Under Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, which of the following is NOT a stated condition for a valid Hindu marriage?
o: The bridegroom and bride have completed 21 and 18 years respectively.
The parties must belong to the same sub-caste.
The parties are not within the prohibited degrees of relationship.
Neither party has a living spouse at the time of marriage.
accepted.x: Belonging to the same sub-caste is not a condition under Section 5. The section includes conditions relating to a living spouse, age, prohibited degrees and sapinda relationship, subject to custom in the last case.
accepted.tq: Separate statutory conditions from a social practice not included in the provision.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding a second marriage under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955:
1. A second marriage during the lifetime of a living spouse is void.
2. Such a marriage may attract punishment for bigamy under Section 494 of the IPC.
3. Section 11 of the Act is associated with the voidness of such a marriage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct: the second marriage is void under Section 11 and may constitute bigamy punishable under Section 494 of the IPC.
accepted.tq: Use the linked provision, legal consequence and penal provision together.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s:
Arrange the following marriage-related enactments in chronological order:
A. Special Marriage Act
B. Hindu Marriage Act
C. Anand Marriage Act
D. Foreign Marriage Act
o: C, A, B, D
A, C, B, D
C, B, A, D
A, B, C, D
accepted.x: The Anand Marriage Act was enacted in 1909, the Special Marriage Act in 1954, the Hindu Marriage Act in 1955 and the Foreign Marriage Act in 1969.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest enactment first and then place the 1954, 1955 and 1969 statutes.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Anand Marriage Act — 1909; registration added in 2012
Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act — 1969
Foreign Marriage Act — 1939
Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act — 1939
accepted.x: The Anand Marriage Act was enacted in 1909 and registration was added in 2012. The Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act is of 1939, the Foreign Marriage Act is of 1969 and the Parsi Act is of 1936.
accepted.tq: Use statute-year discrimination among closely related marriage enactments.
accepted.sec: Acts governing marriage - SMA 1872, SMA 1954, HMA 1955, Goa civil code (age, conditions, polygamy)

accepted.s: An upper-caste man marrying a lower-caste woman is described as:
o: Anuloma
Sambandham
Pratiloma
Niyoga
accepted.x: Anuloma, or hypergamy, refers to the marriage of an upper-caste man with a lower-caste woman.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two opposite caste-direction terms.
accepted.sec: Types of marriages in the Vedic period and customary unions (Anuloma, Pratiloma, Sambandham, Niyoga)

accepted.s: Pratiloma marriage refers to:
o: An upper-caste man marrying a lower-caste woman
A widow marrying her husband's brother
A widower marrying his wife's sister
A lower-caste man marrying a higher-caste woman
accepted.x: Pratiloma denotes the marriage of a lower-caste man with a higher-caste woman and was traditionally condemned.
accepted.tq: Reverse the direction of Anuloma carefully rather than relying on similar-sounding terms.
accepted.sec: Types of marriages in the Vedic period and customary unions (Anuloma, Pratiloma, Sambandham, Niyoga)

accepted.s: Sambandham was traditionally associated with:
o: A marriage acquired by service at the bride's home
A widow's marriage with her husband's brother among Gonds
A formal monogamous marriage under the Special Marriage Act
A consensual informal union among Namboothiris and Nairs under Kerala's matrilineal system
accepted.x: Sambandham was a consensual and informal union associated with Namboothiris and Nairs under Kerala's matrilineal system.
accepted.tq: Identify the regional community and social setting linked to the customary union.
accepted.sec: Types of marriages in the Vedic period and customary unions (Anuloma, Pratiloma, Sambandham, Niyoga)

accepted.s: Niyoga traditionally involved:
o: A bride being obtained through exchange between two families
A wife cohabiting with a designated man to beget a child when her husband was impotent or dead
A husband marrying his wife's sister after her death
A lower-caste man marrying a higher-caste woman
accepted.x: Niyoga permitted a wife to cohabit with a designated man for begetting a child when her husband was impotent or dead.
accepted.tq: Apply the definition to the family situation described in the question.
accepted.sec: Types of marriages in the Vedic period and customary unions (Anuloma, Pratiloma, Sambandham, Niyoga)

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Levirate — widower marries his wife's sister
Sororate — widow marries her husband's brother
Levirate — widow marries her husband's brother
Niyoga — widower marries his wife's sister
accepted.x: Levirate is the marriage of a widow with her deceased husband's brother. Sororate refers to a widower marrying his wife's sister.
accepted.tq: Separate the widow-brother relationship from the widower-sister relationship.
accepted.sec: Types of marriages in the Vedic period and customary unions (Anuloma, Pratiloma, Sambandham, Niyoga)

accepted.s: Which one of the following trends is associated with the Later Vedic period?
o: Swayamvara became increasingly dominant and widow remarriage was encouraged.
Child marriage emerged, Swayamvara declined and widow remarriage was discouraged.
Marriage within the same gotra became compulsory.
All restrictions on marriage within the same gotra were removed.
accepted.x: The Later Vedic period saw the emergence of child marriage, decline of Swayamvara, discouragement of widow remarriage and prohibition of marriage within the same gotra.
accepted.tq: Recognise the cluster of social changes rather than an isolated reversal.
accepted.sec: Types of marriages in the Vedic period and customary unions (Anuloma, Pratiloma, Sambandham, Niyoga)

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT listed as a traditional way of acquiring a mate among tribal communities?
o: Capture
Exchange
Probation
Compulsory registration under the Hindu Marriage Act
accepted.x: Probation, capture and exchange were listed among the ways of acquiring a mate. Compulsory registration under the Hindu Marriage Act was not such a tribal form.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional legal procedure that does not belong to the customary list.
accepted.sec: Tribal forms of marriage → tribe, tribal terms (Diku Andi, Diku Amol)

accepted.s: Capture as a form of acquiring a mate has been associated with which of the following groups?
o: Namboothiri, Nair, Parsi and Sikh
Gond, Munda, Nair and Ho only
Rajasthan, Kerala, Goa and Punjab
Naga, Ho, Bhil and Gond
accepted.x: Capture marriage is associated with the Naga, Ho, Bhil and Gond communities.
accepted.tq: Recall the complete community list without substituting communities linked to other forms.
accepted.sec: Tribal forms of marriage → tribe, tribal terms (Diku Andi, Diku Amol)

accepted.s: In the service form of acquiring a mate, the groom traditionally:
o: Obtains the bride only through capture
Exchanges his sister for the bride in every case
Proves his eligibility through a written examination
Works at the bride's home, as reported among the Gonds
accepted.x: Among the Gonds, the groom may work at the bride's home as a form of service associated with acquiring a mate.
accepted.tq: Match the described conduct with the correct tribal marriage form.
accepted.sec: Tribal forms of marriage → tribe, tribal terms (Diku Andi, Diku Amol)

accepted.s: The trial form of acquiring a mate traditionally involves:
o: Payment of a fixed bride price by the groom
Exchange of two brides between villages
Marriage only after seven years of separation
Demonstration of prowess in a dance game
accepted.x: In the trial form, the prospective groom demonstrates prowess in a dance game.
accepted.tq: Distinguish trial by prowess from service, purchase and exchange.
accepted.sec: Tribal forms of marriage → tribe, tribal terms (Diku Andi, Diku Amol)

accepted.s: Youth dormitories in tribal societies traditionally provided:
o: A system of marriage exclusively through capture
A prohibition on interaction between unmarried persons
A compulsory arrangement of marriages by elders
A wide choice of mates through mutual consent
accepted.x: Youth dormitories gave young people a wide choice of mates through mutual consent.
accepted.tq: Test the social function of youth dormitories rather than confusing it with a coercive form.
accepted.sec: Tribal forms of marriage → tribe, tribal terms (Diku Andi, Diku Amol)

accepted.s: The Atta Satta practice refers to:
o: A marriage within the same gotra
A Kerala matrilineal union
Marriage by service among the Gonds
Bride exchange in Rajasthan
accepted.x: Atta Satta is a bride-exchange practice in Rajasthan, which was criticised by the Rajasthan High Court.
accepted.tq: Identify the regional customary practice and distinguish it from other tribal forms.
accepted.sec: Tribal forms of marriage → tribe, tribal terms (Diku Andi, Diku Amol)

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a ground for divorce under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955?
o: Adultery
Conversion
Cruelty
Irretrievable breakdown of marriage as an express statutory ground
accepted.x: Adultery, cruelty and conversion are grounds under Section 13. Irretrievable breakdown is not an express statutory ground under the Hindu Marriage Act.
accepted.tq: Separate listed statutory grounds from a ground recognised through constitutional judicial power.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s: Which one of the following is included among the grounds for divorce under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955?
o: The marriage was solemnised under civil law
The parties belong to different villages
The parties follow different occupations
The spouse has not been heard of for seven years
accepted.x: A spouse not having been heard of for seven years is one of the grounds stated under Section 13.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive time-based statutory ground.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s: Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 deals with:
o: Marriage within prohibited degrees
Divorce by mutual consent
Registration of Parsi marriages
Void marriages due to bigamy
accepted.x: Section 13B provides for divorce by mutual consent.
accepted.tq: Match the exact section with its subject.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding irretrievable breakdown of marriage:
1. It is not an express statutory ground under the Hindu Marriage Act.
2. The Supreme Court may grant relief on this basis under Article 142.
3. The Supreme Court in Naveen Kohli (2006) urged that it be made a statutory ground.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Irretrievable breakdown is not a statutory ground, but the Supreme Court can use Article 142, and Naveen Kohli urged legislative recognition of the ground.
accepted.tq: Combine the statutory position, constitutional power and leading judgment.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s: In which case did the Supreme Court hold instant triple talaq to be unconstitutional?
o: Shayara Bano
Sarla Mudgal
Naveen Kohli v. Neelu Kohli
Kesavananda Bharati
accepted.x: The Supreme Court held instant triple talaq unconstitutional in Shayara Bano (2017).
accepted.tq: Identify the judgment specifically associated with the constitutional status of instant triple talaq.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s: The Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 provides that instant triple talaq is:
o: Valid but subject only to civil compensation
Void and illegal, with punishment of up to three years' imprisonment and fine
A ground available only to the husband and not regulated by law
Valid if pronounced before witnesses
accepted.x: The 2019 Act makes instant triple talaq void and illegal and provides for imprisonment of up to three years along with fine. It also provides for subsistence allowance and custody-related relief.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the legal status and penal consequence from the earlier personal-law position.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the remedies available to a Muslim wife for seeking divorce?
o: Only unilateral talaq by the husband
Khula by mutual consent and grounds under the Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act, 1939
Only a remedy before a Family Court under the Special Marriage Act
Only divorce under Section 13B of the Hindu Marriage Act
accepted.x: A Muslim wife may seek khula by mutual consent and may invoke the Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act, 1939. Grounds include lack of maintenance for two years, imprisonment of seven or more years and cruelty.
accepted.tq: Match the legal routes with the community-specific law and avoid importing provisions from another statute.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s: Which of the following is a ground mentioned in the Dissolution of Muslim Marriage Act, 1939?
o: The wife belongs to a different gotra
The parties reside in different villages
The marriage was solemnised under the Anand Marriage Act
The husband has failed to provide maintenance for two years
accepted.x: Failure of the husband to provide maintenance for two years is among the grounds mentioned. Other cited grounds include imprisonment of seven or more years and cruelty.
accepted.tq: Recall the precise duration attached to the maintenance-based ground.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s: The Family Courts Act was enacted in:
accepted.x: The Family Courts Act was enacted in 1984.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the enactment year from the years of the principal marriage and divorce statutes.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s: As of 31 July 2025, the number of Family Courts was:
accepted.x: There were 953 Family Courts as of 31 July 2025.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact current-affairs figure and date together.
accepted.sec: Divorce - definitions, HMA grounds, triple talaq law and judgments, Family Courts Act

accepted.s: Endogamy refers to:
o: Marriage only between persons of different religions
Marriage between a widow and her husband's brother
Marriage within a specified social group such as a varna, caste or sub-caste
Marriage outside one's gotra or clan
accepted.x: Endogamy operates at the varna, caste and sub-caste levels and requires marriage within the specified group.
accepted.tq: Contrast endogamy with exogamy by focusing on whether marriage is within or outside the group.
accepted.sec: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes exogamy in relation to gotra?
o: It requires marriage within one's own gotra.
It permits marriage only within the same sub-caste.
It bars marriage within one's own gotra.
It is identical to hypergamy.
accepted.x: Exogamy bars marriage within one's own gotra. It therefore operates as a rule requiring marriage outside the specified gotra group.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of the marriage rule and avoid reversing endogamy and exogamy.
accepted.sec: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees

accepted.s: Ghurye regarded which of the following as the defining feature of caste?
o: Sororate
Endogamy
Exogamy
Niyoga
accepted.x: Ghurye identified endogamy as the defining feature of caste.
accepted.tq: Associate the sociologist with the distinctive analytical proposition.
accepted.sec: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees

accepted.s: Which combination best describes the traditional rules of mate selection in North India?
o: Caste endogamy, clan endogamy and village endogamy
Caste endogamy, clan or gotra exogamy and village exogamy
Caste exogamy, clan exogamy and village endogamy
Caste exogamy, clan endogamy and village endogamy
accepted.x: The stated North Indian pattern is caste endogamy, clan or gotra exogamy and village exogamy.
accepted.tq: Keep the three levels separate and compare the direction of each marriage rule.
accepted.sec: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees

accepted.s: The sasan rule in North India bars marriage with:
o: Only members of the same sub-caste
All persons belonging to another village
The patri-family and sapinda kin
Only persons belonging to a different religion
accepted.x: The sasan rule bars marriage with members of the patri-family and with sapinda kin.
accepted.tq: Identify the two relationships covered by the customary rule.
accepted.sec: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees

accepted.s: Under Section 3(f) of the Hindu Marriage Act, the sapinda relationship extends to:
o: Three generations on the mother's side and five on the father's side
Five generations on the mother's side and three on the father's side
Two generations on the mother's side and three on the father's side
Three generations on both sides
accepted.x: The sapinda relationship extends to three generations on the mother's side and five generations on the father's side.
accepted.tq: Remember the unequal maternal and paternal generation limits without reversing them.
accepted.sec: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Hypergamy — Pratiloma
Hypogamy — Anuloma
Hypergamy — Anuloma
Exogamy — Niyoga
accepted.x: Hypergamy is Anuloma, while hypogamy is Pratiloma.
accepted.tq: Use the paired synonym relationship to distinguish the two opposite marriage directions.
accepted.sec: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees

accepted.s: Who analysed the concepts of sapinda and gotra?
o: Irawati Karve
R. Ambedkar
M. N. Srinivas
G. S. Ghurye
accepted.x: Karve analysed the concepts of sapinda and gotra.
accepted.tq: Match the scholar with the specific concepts associated with the analysis.
accepted.sec: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees

accepted.s: The Delhi High Court upheld which provision of the Hindu Marriage Act in relation to the sapinda bar?
o: Section 5(v)
Section 13B
Section 5(i)
Section 5(iii)
accepted.x: The Delhi High Court upheld Section 5(v), which concerns the sapinda restriction, subject to the statutory framework regarding custom.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact clause number associated with the judicially upheld restriction.
accepted.sec: Rules of mate selection - endogamy, exogamy, gotra and sapinda, hypergamy, hypogamy, prohibited degrees
